fact: L'Economie reports taxpayers declare on the E-Tax platform, and the Fouta pilot was run among firms already familiar with online declaration.

L'Economie reports that since 3 August 2026 taxpayers pay taxes and levies online through the Fouta national switch after declaring on E-Tax, with an electronic Treasury receipt, rollout to all taxpayers by end of 2026.

The Ministry of Finance says the FOUTA online tax payment platform is being deployed in three phases, with a pilot phase engaged, large and medium enterprises next, and all taxpayers by the end of 2026.
The Ministry of Finance says the FOUTA pilot phase was engaged with a number of enterprises that already file returns electronically (telediclaration), with the declaration made on E-Tax.

The Ministry of Finance says taxes are paid online through FOUTA after declaration on E-Tax, by mobile money or bank transfer validated by OTP, with a signed electronic receipt, and a live payment demonstration was given on 3 July 2026 (pilot phase).
The Treasury sheet names E-TAX, a tax and duties management system built in-house by the finance ministry, among reforms launched to collect revenue better.
Congo's finance ministry demonstrated Fouta online tax and customs declaration and payment to deputies on 23 June 2026, without stating it is in service.
MTN Congo's page says taxpayers create an account on impots.gouv.cg and fill in their tax declaration online.
MTN Congo's page says the e-tax declaration is paid through the payment-method step by choosing MTN Mobile Money, free of charge, from 1 to 750,000 FCFA.
The ministry says e-Tax, run by the tax directorate, is the online filing and payment system for domestic taxes, and it brought in 94 billion FCFA via Fouta from June to 16 November 2026.
The ministry says taxes are paid online through e-Tax, with 94 billion FCFA collected via Fouta by 16 November 2026.
Yoka said FCFA 94 billion of tax revenue was collected through e-Tax via the FOUTA payment platform between 1 June and 16 November 2026.
